evals.prompt: You are the Task Generator. Read the agent prompt at `.planning/agents/task-generator.md`. Then read `.planning/behavioral-spec.json` and `.planning/technical-spec.json`. There is no codebase audit (this is a new project). Generate all task files and the manifest.
evals.expected_output: A manifest.json and individual task JSON files in .planning/tasks/. Tasks should cover all 5 scenarios and all 4 technical decisions. Each task is a vertical slice with scenarios, decisions, files, and assumptions.
expectations: At least one task file is created per scenario group in .planning/tasks/
Every scenario ID (SC-01 through SC-05) appears in at least one task's scenarios array
Every decision area from the technical spec appears in at least one task's decisions array
No task's files array contains test files — test_files is always empty at generation time
The dependency graph is acyclic — no circular depends_on references
Every task has a short imperative title, not 'Task 1' or similar generic names
Tasks that are referenced in other tasks' depends_on have a non-empty assumptions array
Every scenario's Then clause is concrete enough to be translated into a failing test
No task references another task by ID in its files, scenarios, decisions, or notes

evals.prompt: You are the Task Generator. Read the agent prompt at `.planning/agents/task-generator.md`. Then read `.planning/behavioral-spec.json`, `.planning/technical-spec.json`, and `.planning/technical-vision.md`. There is no codebase audit. Generate all task files and the manifest. Pay attention to the engineer's reasoning in the technical vision when writing task notes.
evals.expected_output: Same task structure as eval 1, but task notes should incorporate context from the technical vision where relevant — for instance, the debounce reasoning for search, or the optimistic update pattern for delete.
expectations: All validation checks from eval 1 still pass (coverage, acyclicity, self-containment)
At least one task's notes field references context from the technical vision (e.g., debounce timing, optimistic update pattern, or React Query cache invalidation strategy)
The technical vision does NOT override the locked decisions in the technical spec — decisions arrays contain technical spec decisions only
Task files reference .planning/codebase/ documents in codebase_context only if a codebase audit exists (empty array for new projects)

evals.prompt: You are the Task Generator. Read the agent prompt at `.planning/agents/task-generator.md`. Then read `.planning/behavioral-spec.json` and `.planning/technical-spec.json`. Generate tasks. Specifically verify: are the tasks appropriately sized? No task should be too large (implementing the entire feature) or too small (only a migration with nothing verifiable).
evals.expected_output: Tasks are vertical slices — each touches multiple layers and delivers something independently verifiable. No single task implements all 5 scenarios. No task only creates a database table without corresponding API or UI code.
expectations: No single task contains all 5 scenarios — work is split across multiple tasks
No task's files array has more than 10 entries
Every task's files array includes files across multiple layers (not just a single migration or a single component)
No task has a files array consisting of only one layer (e.g., only database migrations or only React components) — each task spans at least two layers
